Minecraft: Java Edition, on your phone. This is a fork of Amethyst with a recorder built into the renderer and most of the launcher redrawn.
Record the game, not your screen
Capture happens inside the graphics pipeline, before anything is drawn on top. Your on-screen buttons, notifications and the status bar never appear in the video — just the game.
Not available on the Zink renderer, and a clip stops before 4 GB — around 40 minutes at 1080p60.
Home, settings, sign-in, profiles, the version picker and the in-game menu were redrawn from scratch — designed around what you actually do, and built to work one-handed.
When the game dies, the log gets read for you and the cause is named — a missing mod dependency, not enough memory, the wrong Java version — with the line it concluded from.
A real on-screen keyboard instead of a list of keycodes. Hold a key down to keep it there, so F3 + G finally works, and type straight into chat.

The game filled everything the Memory allocation setting allows, and Java shut it down.
Raise Memory allocation in Settings → Performance if the phone has room — or lower render distance, resolution, or the mod count so the game needs less.
The phone ran out of memory
Java asked the phone for more memory than it could give.
Lower Memory allocation in Settings → Performance, and close other apps before playing.
The system force-closed the game\'s process, which usually means the phone ran out of memory.
Wrong Java version for this Minecraft
This Minecraft needs a newer Java than the one the profile launched with.
This Minecraft is built for Java %1$d, but the profile launched with Java %2$d.
In the profile\'s settings, switch Runtime to a newer Java — install one first from Settings → Performance → Runtime Manager if none is listed.
This Forge needs an older Java
Forge versions this old only run on Java 8, and the profile launched with something newer.
In the profile\'s settings, switch Runtime to a Java 8 runtime.
A mod is missing something it needs
Fabric stopped the launch because a mod\'s requirements aren\'t installed.
The lines under “Unmet dependency listing” in the log name the mod and what it wants. Install that, or remove the mod.
The log\'s suggested fix: install %1$s. Put it in the mods folder and launch again.
Forge stopped the launch because a mod depends on another mod that isn\'t installed.
Forge stopped the launch because “%1$s” needs “%2$s”, which isn\'t installed.
Install the missing mod, or remove the one that asks for it.
The same mod is installed twice
Two copies of one mod are in the mods folder, and the loader refuses to choose.
Two copies of “%1$s” are in the mods folder, and the loader refuses to choose.
Open the mods folder under Game files and delete the older copy.
A mod doesn\'t match this Minecraft
A mod tried to hook into game code that isn\'t there — usually a mod built for a different Minecraft or loader version.
Update or remove the mod named in the log line below. After changing Minecraft versions, every mod needs a matching build.
The renderer couldn\'t create or keep an OpenGL context on this device.
Pick a different Renderer in Settings → Performance — it\'s saved per profile, so trying each one is safe.
The phone is out of storage
Minecraft tried to write a file and the system refused: no space left on the device.
Free some space — old recordings and unused apps are the usual suspects — then launch again.
Minecraft\'s servers rejected this account\'s session.
Open the account switcher on the home screen and sign in to the account again.
No connection to the download servers
Something the launch needed couldn\'t be fetched over the network.
Check the connection and launch again — once a version is fully downloaded, it starts without internet.
A file this version depends on is incomplete or unreadable — usually the leftovers of an interrupted download.
Delete this version\'s folder inside Game files → versions, then launch again to re-download it cleanly.
Native code — most often the graphics driver — hit an error it couldn\'t recover from.
Try a different Renderer in Settings → Performance. If every renderer crashes the same way, share the log.
The log doesn\'t show a known cause
The game ended without leaving one of the failure patterns this launcher recognises.
The answer is usually in the last lines of the log — share it, or open latestlog.txt under Game files.
